channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Fim da 6x1 cria dilema fatal para Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The end of the 6x1 workweek creates division in the Senate, with senators calling the measure innocuous and election-driven, warning of economic risks. Supporters highlight the benefit of extra time for workers' families. The debate reflects parliamentary tensions over labor reforms.

item.title: Tarcísio tenta manter 'distância estratégica' de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas publicly supports Flávio Bolsonaro but avoids joint events in contentious areas, focusing on controlled gatherings. Allies of the senator criticize the governor for lacking engagement in the shared campaign efforts.

item.title: Número de candidatos a governador cai; SP lidera queda e Minas vai na contramão
item.description: The average number of gubernatorial candidates in the 2026 elections dropped to 7.2 per state, compared to 8.3 in 2022 and 7.6 in 2018. São Paulo records the lowest number in its history (7 candidates), while Minas Gerais leads the increase, rising from 8 to 11 candidates. Political coordination during the pre-campaign, such as the 'scare-off' effect, directly influences the number of candidacies in each state.

item.title: Eleições 2026: veja as datas do primeiro e segundo turno
item.description: The 2026 elections in Brazil will be held in two rounds: the first on October 4th, covering federal and state deputies, senators, governors, and the president. The second round, if needed, will take place on October 25th, only for the presidential and gubernatorial races where no candidate reaches over 50% of valid votes in the first round.

item.title: Nikolas Ferreira quer eleger ‘exército’ de aliados para ampliar influência política
item.description: Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) aims to build a parallel bench with candidates in every Brazilian state, strengthening his political influence in Congress and the Minas Gerais legislature. While the PL manages internal conflicts involving Michelle and Flávio Bolsonaro, Ferreira focuses on creating a loyal and ideologically aligned team.

item.title: Lulinha disse a lobista que viagem em grupo à Europa era “arriscada”
item.description: Federal Police messages reveal that Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, opposed a group trip to Europe organized by a lobbyist, citing risks and suggesting postponement. Investigations indicate destinations such as Switzerland and Liechtenstein, with purposes including bank account openings and potential financial obfuscation.

item.title: 'Taxa das blusinhas', fim da 6x1, terras raras: Lula tenta destravar pautas do governo em reunião com Alcolumbre e Motta
item.description: Lula meets with Alcolumbre and Motta to discuss approving agendas including end of 6x1 scale, public security, rare earths and review of fees on low-value imports.

item.title: STF faz audiência pública sobre combate a facções criminosas; Lei Antifacção é questionada na Corte
item.description: The STF holds a public hearing to debate the constitutionality of the Anti-Gang Law, which faces four lawsuits filed by legal associations and the Public Ministry. Justices advocate for inter-institutional cooperation to combat organized crime in a coordinated manner, criticizing the current fragmented approach to public security. The law was signed by President Lula in March this year.

item.title: Deepfake nas eleições: entenda o que é e por que pode enganar o eleitor
item.description: Deepfakes are manipulated images or audio created using AI that can mislead voters, spreading false content and eroding trust in real media. The TSE banned their use in electoral campaigns starting in 2024, imposing strict restrictions during election periods. Sharing deepfakes may lead to legal consequences if intentional misinformation or fraud is proven.

item.title: Escala 6x1: Relator descarta mudanças e diz que trabalha para votar texto em comissão do Senado na próxima semana
item.description: The rapporteur of the PEC ending the 6x1 work schedule in the Senate, Senator Omar Aziz, stated he will not make changes to the text and plans to vote the report at the CCJ next week, advancing to plenary consideration between August 31 and September 4. The proposal reduces the weekly work hours from 44 to 42 in two months, without salary cuts. Lula pressures for approval before the October municipal elections.

item.title: Flávio desembarca em Alagoas para estreia no Nordeste com ausências esperadas de JHC e Lira
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro kicks off his presidential campaign in the Northeast with a stop in Alagoas, but faces challenges without the backing of JHC and Arthur Lira. Despite being the running mate in Alagoas, the senator arrives in the state without uniting key local figures, reflecting difficulties in building alliances where Lula leads significantly.

item.title: Propostas de presidenciáveis priorizam reação à prevenção da violência contra crianças, diz Unicef
item.description: The Unicef analyzed the government plans of the five main 2026 presidential candidates and found that, while proposals against violence toward children and adolescents exist, most prioritize punitive responses (such as increased penalties and policing) over preventive actions. Candidates like Lula and Caiado focus on combating violence, whereas Zema, Bolsonaro, and Renan emphasize education. The report underscores the need for preventive social policies to effectively protect children and adolescents.

item.title: Erika desafia Flávio para debate sobre 6x1: “Vai aceitar ou passar mal?”
item.description: Federal deputy Erika Hilton (PSol-SP) challenged Senator and presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) to a public debate on the PEC proposing the end of the 6×1 work schedule. The invitation was made on social media after a O Globo report indicated that Flávio's allies are trying to block the PEC in Congress.

item.title: Como foi o debate da Band: Caiado, Renan e Cury disparam ataques contra Lula e Flávio; veja repercussão
item.description: In the first presidential debate on Band, Caiado, Renan and Cury attacked Lula and Flávio, while the event was the emptiest since 1989. Lula gave an interview to Record and Flávio released an alternative video. The main debates focused on economy, security and corruption.

item.title: Coordenador de campanha de Lula defende recompra de títulos da dívida e alta de imposto para super-ricos
item.description: José Sergio Gabrielli, Lula's (PT) campaign coordinator, advocates for government intervention in public debt markets to lower long-term interest rates and suggests higher taxes for the wealthy. These measures aim to stabilize the economy and promote wealth redistribution.

item.title: O que Romeu Zema disse em sabatina do Jornal Nacional com presidenciáveis
item.description: Romeu Zema, candidate from the New Party, participated in a Jornal Nacional town hall, promising to privatize state-owned companies, classify criminal factions as terrorist organizations, and grant amnesty to those convicted in connection with the January 8, 2023 events. The interview was the first of six scheduled with presidential candidates this week.

item.title: Zema diz que tribunais fazem “mais política do que justiça”
item.description: Presidential candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) stated in an interview with Jornal Nacional that Brazilian courts are acting with political bias, particularly in STF judgments regarding the January 8th events and Jair Bolsonaro's conviction. He advocated for pardoning the defendants and questioned whether the incidents constituted a coup attempt, calling the convictions a 'clearly political trial.' Despite his remarks, he emphasized trust in electronic voting and commitment to democracy.

item.title: Janja repudia críticas de Renan Santos feitas em debate na “Band”
item.description: First Lady Janja da Silva publicly rejected criticisms made by Renan Santos during a presidential debate on TV Band, accusing him of personal and derogatory attacks against her and women in general. She also referenced a previous incident where Renan joked about rape, reinforcing her condemnation of misogynistic and violent rhetoric.

item.title: Vice de Zema diz não levar pesquisas “muito a sério”
item.description: Senator Eduardo Girao, running for vice president under Romeu Zema, stated he does not take electoral polls seriously and denied they influenced his decision not to run for Ceara state government. He highlighted the discrepancy between poll intentions and actual election results, using his own 2018 Senate race as an example. Girao also reaffirmed support for Zema's agenda, emphasizing tax cuts and privatizations.

item.title: Fim da escala 6 X 1 terá mais de 65 votos, estima Aziz
item.description: Omar Aziz (PSD-AM), rapporteur of the PEC 221, estimates over 65 votes in favor of ending the 6X1 shift, which reduces the weekly work schedule from 44 to 40 hours and grants 2 weekly rest days. The proposal will be presented on Wednesday and voted on at the Senate’s CCJ on September 2, 2026, without plans to amend its content. Despite approval in the Chamber, Aziz notes no senator opposition and emphasizes President Lula's support for the measure.

item.title: Janja repudia “ataque pessoal e depreciativo” de Renan em debate: “Misoginia”
item.description: First lady Janja Lula da Silva condemned statements made by candidate Renan Santos during the first 2026 presidential debate, labeling them as personal and misogynistic attacks. In a statement sent to Band, Janja argued that Renan used her figure to target President Lula, pointing to a pattern of disrespect toward women. The debate was marked by the absence of three candidates, including Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Romeu Zema.

item.title: Flávio aciona TSE contra Durigan por atuação de ministro em campanha
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) filed a lawsuit with the TSE against Finance Minister Dario Durigan, accusing him of using the Ministry's structure to support Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's (PT) reelection. The filing cites media reports and official events where Durigan allegedly acted as Lula's economic spokesperson, suggesting improper use of public administration for campaign purposes. Flávio's lawyers ask the TSE to preserve related documents and bar the minister from using public resources for future engagements.

item.title: 'Tenho uma série de programas contra as mulheres': gafe de Zema durante entrevista à TV Globo repercute nas redes
item.description: Presidential candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) made a gaffe by stating he has 'a series of programs against women' during a TV Globo interview on violence against women. His proposals include expanding specialized police stations, shelters, and electronic ankle bracelets. The statement was widely criticized on social media.

item.title: Zema: Tornar vacinação obrigatória não é o que pode acontecer num país democrático
item.description: Romeu Zema, candidate from the New Party for the Presidency, stated he is against mandatory vaccination, deeming it undemocratic, during an interview with Jornal Nacional. Despite being fully vaccinated himself, he advocates for individual freedom.

item.title: Zema já admite manter valorização do mínimo e quer esperar para alterar idade para aposentar
item.description: In a TV Globo interview, Romeu Zema (Novo) admitted he might keep the minimum wage increase and hesitated on raising the retirement age, signaling flexibility in his fiscal adjustment plan. He also avoided taking a firm stance on structural reforms, opting to wait for more economic context.

item.title: Zema, sobre salário mínimo: Garanto que ninguém vai ter perda; se tiver inflação, nós daremos
item.description: Romeu Zema, candidate of the Novo party for the Presidency, stated that he will ensure inflation-adjusted minimum wage increases, without harm to workers, if elected. In an interview with Jornal Nacional, he reiterated there will be no loss in the minimum wage and any inflation impact will be offset.

item.title: Quaest: veja como está a disputa entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro em AL, MA, PR, RN, RS e SC
item.description: Quaest released polling data for the presidential race in six Brazilian states (AL, MA, PR, RN, RS, SC), showing the contest between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro. Results vary by region, reflecting distinct voter profiles. Coverage focuses solely on vote intentions, without platform analysis.

item.title: Flávio: Vou montar um time de ministros competentes, como a Daniella Marques que está aqui
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, PL candidate for President of Brazil, announced his intention to form a team of competent ministers if elected, citing former Caixa Econômica Federal president Daniella Marques as an example. He emphasized the importance of having qualified professionals in the government team.

item.title: Pesquisa indica a dificuldade duradoura na campanha eleitoral de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign faces challenges with female voters, according to BTG Pactual/Nexus research. Lula leads among women with 48% voting intentions against Flávio's 31%, while the scenario reverses among men. The issue is linked to Jair Bolsonaro's image and Michelle Bolsonaro's absence from events.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro pede para manter publicação de vídeo com críticas a Lulinha
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) is facing a defamation lawsuit filed by Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, over an AI-generated video accusing the businessman of stealing millions from the elderly. Lulinha's legal team argues the video, while using humor elements, presents a false accusation as fact. Flávio seeks to keep the video online, classifying it as political satire.

item.title: Janja repudia fala de Renan Santos em debate presidencial da Band e do Estadão: ‘Caráter misógino’
item.description: Janja da Silva condemned Renan Santos' remarks during a presidential debate, labeling them as misogynistic and used to attack President Lula. Renan suggested depreciatingly that Lula was with 'that Janja' and could find 'better company'. The first lady emphasized that the comment is not political criticism but an attempt to ridicule women.

item.title: Zema não garante aumento real do salário mínimo e diz que, 'por ora', não mexeria em idades de aposentadoria
item.description: Romeu Zema stated that if elected, he will only ensure inflation adjustment for the minimum wage without committing to real increases, and has no immediate plans to change retirement ages, tying future reforms to economic performance and labor market formalization.

item.title: Quem são os candidatos ao Senado por Goiás (GO) nas eleições 2026
item.description: In the 2026 elections, Goiás will elect two new federal senators, with ELEVEN confirmed pre-candidates. Key names include Vanderlan Cardoso (PSD), seeking re-election, and Gracinha Caiado (União), former first lady of the state. The race will be decided in a single round on October 4th, for seats previously held by Jorge Kajuru and Vanderlan Cardoso.

item.title: Quaest: em SC, Flávio Bolsonaro tem 45% e Lula 20% no 1º turno
item.description: A Quaest poll in Santa Catarina shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leading with 45% against Lula (PT) at 20% in the first round of 2026. Pablo Marçal (PRTB) does not significantly change the scenario, holding 2% of voting intention. The margin of error is 3 points, with 13% undecided and 8% blank/null votes.

item.title: Erika Hilton “desafia” Flávio a debater fim da escala 6 X 1
item.description: Federal deputy Erika Hilton (Psol-SP) challenged senator and presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro to a public debate on the PEC proposing the end of the 6 X 1 work schedule, following a O Globo report accusing Flávio of mobilizing Senate allies to delay the vote. The PEC, filed by Erika in 2024, has government support and divides opinion in the opposition. The vote is scheduled for September 2nd at the Senate CCJ.

item.title: No JN, Zema comete gafe e diz que tem “série de programas contra mulheres”
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) made a gaffe during a Jornal Nacional interview by saying he has 'a series of programs against women,' when referring to measures to combat violence against women. The statement was widely criticized on social media as a major misstep, though Zema later clarified that the initiatives include expanding specialized police stations, creating shelters for domestic violence victims, and using electronic ankle bracelets for offenders. He also advocated for awareness programs in schools and was questioned about Minas Gerais' public debt, which he attributed to inherited liabilities from previous administrations.

item.title: Em "Dark Horse" e Lulinha, Justiça não é cega; enxerga com um olho só
item.description: The text criticizes the perception of partiality in the Brazilian justice system, suggesting that investigations against political figures such as Lula and those involved in the 'Dark Horse' case are influenced by electoral motives. It questions the impartiality of ministers and media pressure on judicial decisions, advocating for greater transparency in investigations.

item.title: Eleições 2026 – Romeu Zema responde a pergunta sobre anistia a condenados pelo 8 de janeiro
item.description: Romeu Zema, during the 2026 elections, was questioned about the possibility of amnesty for those convicted in connection with the January 8th attack on the National Congress. He avoided taking a clear stance, suggesting that judicial decisions should be respected.

item.title: PF investiga operador financeiro de amiga de Lulinha para saques e pagamentos em dinheiro vivo
item.description: Federal Police investigate financial operator Ulisses Barbosa, accused of facilitating cash withdrawals and payments for lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, possibly covering flights of President Lula's son. The investigation raises money laundering suspicions and highlights the use of travel accounts to conceal expenses, with Roberta also probed for influence peddling.

item.title: Veja o que é #FATO e o que é #FAKE na entrevista de Romeu Zema à Globo
item.description: Romeu Zema was the first presidential candidate interviewed by Globo in a series of debates with candidates for the presidency. In the interview, he highlighted the fiscal recovery of Minas Gerais, claiming he took office with a deficit of BRL 11 billion and left with a surplus of BRL 5 billion. The Fact Check team analyzed his statements, verifying the state government's budget data.

item.title: Zema na TV Globo: como o ex-governador se saiu na entrevista? Veja as notas e avaliações dos colunistas do GLOBO
item.description: In his interview with TV Globo, Romeu Zema was criticized for his hesitant and simplistic performance, receiving low scores from columnists. The former governor defended positions close to Bolsonarismo but faced questions about failures in his management in Minas Gerais. The series of debates continues with other presidential candidates.

item.title: Ministro do Brasil e representante do governo Lula aceram reunião na próxima segunda-feira para discutir tarifaço
item.description: The Brazilian Minister of Development, Márcio Elias Rosa, and the U.S. Trade Representative, Jamieson Greer, scheduled a virtual meeting to resume negotiations on tariffs imposed on Brazilian exports. The dialogue was rekindled after a phone call between Presidents Lula and Trump, focusing on potential exemptions from the 25% and 12.5% tariffs.

item.title: O que diz Simone Tebet, na chapa de Haddad, sobre caso Lulinha
item.description: Simone Tebet, PSB candidate for the Senate, stated in an interview with VEJA that suspicions involving President Lula’s son, Fábio Luis, must be investigated swiftly, autonomously, and without double standards. She emphasized equal treatment for all cases, referencing parallel investigations such as that of Flávio Bolsonaro. She denied that her candidacy would be affected by her alliance with Lula, highlighting her independent political trajectory.

item.title: Flávio se esquiva de “Dark Horse” e cobra “follow the money” de Lulinha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro avoided commenting on the accounting of 'Dark Horse' and attacked Fábio Lulinha, son of Lula, demanding transparency about expenses in Spain. During an event at Fiesp, he claimed responsibility is not his and questioned funding for Lulinha. The STF authorized sharing data from the investigation into the film's production company.

item.title: Flávio nega acordo com Tarcísio sobre reeleição
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) denied negotiating with Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) regarding the end of presidential re-election as a condition for greater involvement in the campaign. The statement was made in São Paulo after a meeting with business representatives.

item.title: Zema defende “modelo Bukele” e critica Judiciário “caro e lerdo”
item.description: Presidential candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) said he intends to adopt security measures inspired by Nayib Bukele's model in El Salvador and criticized the judiciary as 'expensive and slow'. In an interview with TV Globo, he argued that 'the place for a criminal is behind bars' and positioned himself as the only candidate with his own proposals for public security.

item.title: Skaf diz que Flávio defende valores da Fiesp, mas evita declarar apoio
item.description: Paulo Skaf, president of Fiesp, praised Flávio Bolsonaro's proposals but avoided declaring formal support, highlighting ideological convergence. During a São Paulo meeting, Flávio advocated for reduced business costs, stronger legal security and technical autonomy in ministries. Skaf emphasized the need to protect Brazilian industry from unfair foreign competition.

item.title: Lula x Flávio: pesquisas mostram como está a disputa presidencial nos estados da região Sul
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro leads in Southern region polls with significant advantages over Lula, especially in Santa Catarina. In all three states, the PL candidate maintains strong voter intentions while Lula struggles to attract voters.

item.title: Lobista amiga de Lulinha recebeu 300 mil em espécie e seria 'costumeiro' pagar passagens de filho do presidente, aponta PF
item.description: The Brazilian Federal Police are investigating President Lula's son, Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger over alleged influence peddling. A report claims Roberta received R$300,000 in cash and paid for Lulinha’s flights. The defendants deny wrongdoing, and their lawyers claim the leaks aim to sway the 2026 election.

item.title: Zema atribui dívida mineira a juros cobrados pela União
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo), a pre-candidate for the presidency, stated in a debate that Minas Gerais' debt to the federal government stems from high interest rates charged by the central government, not new loans during his state tenure.
